channel.title: rzkytmgr
channel.description: A personal portfolio featuring software projects, technical experiments, and engineering write-ups.

item.title: Migrating a Monolith to a Modular Architecture Without Rewriting Everything
item.description: A pragmatic path from tangled monolith to modular monolith — identifying seams, enforcing boundaries with tests, extracting modules one at a time, and avoiding the rewrite trap that kills so many migrations.

item.title: Observability for Small Teams
item.description: How a small team can get real observability without building an observability platform — starting with structured logs and traces, adding the metrics that matter, and designing dashboards around questions instead of charts.

item.title: From Local Development to Production: Creating a Deployment Process Engineers Can Trust
item.description: A detailed overview of building predictable deployment workflows with automated testing, reproducible builds, environment consistency, safe rollouts, monitoring, and reliable rollback strategies.

item.title: Building Reliable Background Job Systems Without Creating Unnecessary Operational Complexity
item.description: A guide to designing dependable background job systems by examining retries, idempotency, scheduling, failure handling, observability, and the trade-offs behind asynchronous processing.

item.title: Why Distributed Systems Become Difficult Even When Every Individual Service Looks Simple
item.description: An examination of how network failures, partial availability, data consistency, coordination, and operational complexity make distributed systems fundamentally different from single-process applications.

item.title: Writing Documentation That Engineers Actually Read
item.description: Why most internal documentation rots, and how to write docs that survive — documenting decisions, keeping examples runnable, writing for the reader's goal, and making documentation part of the review process.

item.title: Measuring Performance Before You Optimize
item.description: A practical guide to performance work that starts with measurements, not guesses — defining baselines, picking the right profiler for the job, avoiding the classic benchmark traps, and knowing when to stop.

item.title: Understanding Database Indexes Through the Lens of Data Structures and Query Planning
item.description: A practical story of a multi-table join that slowed down as data grew, how EXPLAIN revealed the missing index, and the query-planning principles worth carrying forward.

item.title: Designing Software Boundaries That Make Large Applications Easier to Understand
item.description: An exploration of how clear module boundaries can reduce coupling, improve maintainability, and help engineering teams evolve large applications without losing architectural clarity.

item.title: Building Systems That Remain Simple as Product Requirements Continue to Grow
item.description: Why systems drift toward complexity as requirements accumulate, and the working rules — preserving boundaries, measuring before optimizing, and refusing premature complexity — that keep a growing codebase changeable.

item.title: Designing APIs That Evolve Without Breaking Their Consumers
item.description: Practical strategies for evolving public APIs safely — additive changes, compatibility rules, versioning trade-offs, deprecation policies, and the discipline required to keep consumers moving forward without breaking them.
